title: The Night Sky Is Getting Brighter Every Year. Your Dark-Sky Shots Have a Deadline.
excerpt: Satellites said the night was holding steady. Fifty-one thousand people counting stars with their own eyes said otherwise. Artificial sky brightness rose nearly 10 percent a year for a decade, and for night photographers that turns every dark-sky shot into a race against a brightening sky.

title: The Sharpest Lens Is Not Always the Best Lens. Character Is a Choice.
excerpt: Modern lenses are sharper than they have ever been, and somehow the pictures can feel flatter for it. Sigma's new retro 50mm deliberately builds softness back in, and it asks a question every photographer should answer for themselves: when did sharp become the only thing a lens was for?

title: Life Magazine Is Coming Back to Print. Study the Photo Essay, Not Just the Photo.
excerpt: Life magazine taught a country to see the world in pictures, then print let it go. On November 23 it returns with a 250-page first issue, and the lesson for photographers is not nostalgia. It is sequencing: the skill of making pictures work together, which no single hero frame can replace.
